Connection guide
  1. Open this website in desktop Chrome or Edge. If the in-app preview cannot connect, copy its URL into Chrome.
  2. Connect the clock to this Mac with a USB data cable and turn its rear power switch ON. Close other clock or serial software.
  3. For this legacy clock, select 9,600 baud · legacy (or leave Auto selected), then Connect clock. Choose the USB Serial device and allow access. The portal reads settings before enabling writes. Auto checks 57,600 and 9,600 baud; the legacy model does not report a firmware version.
  4. Use Mac time to prepare both clocks, or enter them separately. Each Write button sends only that section.

If no clock response arrives: select 9,600 baud for the legacy model, confirm the front display is lit and the rear power switch is ON, use a data cable, and try a direct USB port. The supplied upgrade guide’s screenshot identifies a CH340 USB adapter; your Mac must expose it as a serial port.

Use Mac time prepares drafts from your system clock. Sync from internet fetches fresh UTC from TimeAPI.io over HTTPS and writes MAN then UTC in one action. MAN uses your Mac’s time zone; this is a one-time sync, not continuous synchronization. Network failures send no time commands and do not fall back to Mac time. The time service receives a normal web request, but no clock settings or USB identifiers. The read response contains one timestamp and the seller app does not establish whether firmware 1.8 returns MAN or UTC. Both time writes are explicit.

This first version supports the seller Chrome App’s sound choices 0–7 and volume 0–8. The printed manual describes additional ranges that are unverified over USB. Firmware updates and front-panel CHR/ET controls are not implemented.

A hosted website connects to the clock attached to the computer running it. Keep this tab open while configuring. No local connection helper is needed when Chrome can see the serial port.
